Processing revenue increased for the fiscal three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the fiscal three months ended September 30, 2025, mainly driven by growth in card revenue of 9.4% from monthly service and risk management fees, improvement in digital and transaction revenue of 13.3% from a higher number of active users on our digital platform and from the ramping up of additional products, as well as a rise in faster payments revenue of 43.8% from expanding transactional volumes.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:5pt;padding-left:18pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Poppins',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Poppins',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.81pt">For the fiscal three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the fiscal three months ended September 30, 2025, core segment revenue increased 7.1%, payments segment revenue increased 9.2%, complementary segment revenue increased 10.4%, and corporate services segment revenue increased 6.2%. style="margin-bottom:5pt;margin-top:15pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-bottom:5pt;margin-top:15pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-bottom:5pt;margin-top:15pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-bottom:5pt;margin-top:15pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-bottom:5pt;margin-top:15pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-bottom:5pt;margin-top:15pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-bottom:5pt;margin-top:15pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-bottom:5pt;margin-top:15pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-bottom:5pt;margin-top:15pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="height:47.25pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><table style="border-collapse:collapse;display:inline-table;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:100.000%"><tr><td style="width:1.0%"></td><td colspan="3" style="border-top:1pt solid #005da6;padding:2.62pt 1pt 1.5pt 1pt;text-align:left;vertical-align:middle"><div style="text-align:right"><font style="color:#1e3767;font-family:'Avenir LT Pro style="min-height:47.25pt;width:100%"><div style="padding-left:31.5pt;text-align:right;text-indent:-31.5pt"><img alt="tech-bluexbara.jpg" src="tech-bluexbara.jpg" style="height:10px;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:816px"><font style="color:#06185f;font-family:'Poppins',sans-serif;font-size:7.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%"><br></font></div><div style="text-align:right"><font style="color:#06185f;font-family:'Poppins',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%"> </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:5pt;margin-top:15pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#06185f;font-family:'Poppins',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Use of Non-GAAP Financial Information</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:5pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Poppins',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) is the term used to refer to the standard framework of guidelines for financial accounting in the United States. GAAP includes the standards, conventions, and rules accountants follow in recording and summarizing transactions in the preparation of financial statements. In addition to reporting financial results in accordance with GAAP, we have provided certain non-GAAP financial measures, including adjusted revenue, adjusted segment revenue, adjusted operating income, adjusted segment income, adjusted cost of revenue, adjusted segment cost of revenue, adjusted operating expenses, adjusted operating margin, adjusted segment income margin, non-GAAP earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (non-GAAP EBITDA), free cash flow, free cash flow conversion,  net operating profit after tax return on invested capital (NOPAT ROIC), and non-GAAP adjusted net income. We also present key revenue, which is the sum of cloud services revenue and processing revenue, and non-key revenue, which is all other GAAP revenue. Key revenue and non-key revenue are components of GAAP revenue and are presented because management views key revenue as the strategic recurring revenue of the business most important for long-term growth.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:5pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Poppins',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We believe non-GAAP financial measures help investors better understand the underlying fundamentals and operating performance of our business. Adjusted revenue, adjusted segment revenue, adjusted operating income, adjusted operating margin, adjusted segment income, adjusted segment income margin, adjusted cost of revenue, adjusted segment cost of revenue, adjusted operating expenses, and adjusted net income eliminate deconversion revenue and associated costs, the gain on assets, net, and an acquisition, which management believes are not indicative of the Company's operating performance. Such adjustments give investors further insight into our performance. Non-GAAP EBITDA is defined as net income attributable to the Company before the effect of interest income, net, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, adjusted for net income before the effect of interest income, net, taxes, depreciation, and amortization attributable to eliminated deconversions, the gain on assets, net, and an acquisition. Free cash flow is defined as net cash from operating activities, less capitalized expenditures, internal use software, and capitalized software, plus proceeds from the sale of assets. NOPAT ROIC is defined as operating income for the trailing four quarters multiplied by one minus the average effective tax rate (ETR) for the trailing four quarters, with the result divided by average invested capital (average of the beginning and ending period balances). Free cash flow conversion is defined as free cash flow, less proceeds from sale of assets, divided by net income.  Management believes that non-GAAP EBITDA is an important measure of the Company&#8217;s overall operating performance and excludes certain costs and other transactions that management does not consider indicative of the Company's ongoing operating performance&#59; free cash flow is useful to measure the funds generated in a given period that are available for debt service requirements and strategic capital decisions&#59; free cash flow conversion is useful to measure the efficiency with which operating results are converted into free cash flow&#59; and NOPAT ROIC is a measure of the Company&#8217;s allocation efficiency and effectiveness of its invested capital. For these reasons, management also uses these non-GAAP financial measures in its assessment and management of the Company's performance.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:5pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Poppins',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Non-GAAP financial measures used by the Company may not be comparable to similarly titled non-GAAP measures used by other companies. Non-GAAP financial measures have no standardized meaning prescribed by GAAP and therefore, are unlikely to be comparable with calculations of similar measures for other companies.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:5pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Poppins',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Any non-GAAP financial measures should be considered in context with the GAAP financial presentation and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for GAAP measures. Reconciliations of the non-GAAP financial measures to related GAAP measures are included.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="height:47.25pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><table included elevated one-time revenues from on-premise implementations and consulting engagements. Excluding those one-time items, growth in key recurring areas of the Core segment grew 8.6%, which is a positive indicator of the ongoing strength of the segment. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Poppins',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">2.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Why did the Company rename &#34;Public and Private Cloud&#34; revenue to &#34;Cloud Services&#34;&#63;</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-left:72pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Poppins',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Poppins',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.45pt">The Company made this change beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 to simplify presentation and improve clarity. This does not represent any change to the products or services we offer or to previously reported financial results, and prior period amounts are presented on a consistent basis.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Poppins',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">3.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;What were the first quarter of fiscal 2026 segment reclassifications&#63; </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-left:72pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Poppins',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Poppins',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.45pt">During the first quarter of fiscal 2027, the Company transferred a product from the Core segment to the Complementary segment for better alignment. Therefore, first quarter of fiscal 2026 results were recast. Revenue of $5,292 and cost of revenue of $746 were reclassified. Other reclassifications unrelated to the product transfer noted above were $757 of cost of revenue reclassified from Core to Corporate Services to align with current allocation of cost of revenue by segment. These changes are segment-level only and do not affect consolidated results.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Poppins',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">4.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;What is the timing of the Connect Conference&#63;</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-left:72pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Poppins',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Poppins',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.45pt">The Connect Conference is Jack Henry's annual client conference. The revenue and expenses associated with the conference are included in the Corporate Services segment.  The event was held in the first quarter of fiscal 2026 and is in the the second quarter of fiscal 2027.  The event will be held in the second quarter for the next four years.</font></div><div style="height:47.25pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><table style="border-collapse:collapse;display:inline-table;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:100.000%"><tr><td style="width:1.0%"></td><td style="width:29.954%"></td><td style="width:0.1%"></td><td style="width:1.0%"></td><td style="width:32.090%"></td><td style="width:0.1%"></td><td style="width:1.0%"></td><td style="width:34.656%"></td><td style="width:0.1%"></td></tr><tr><td colspan="3" style="border-top:1pt solid #005da6;padding:0 1pt;vertical-align:bottom"><div><img alt="jack-henryxwordmark2.jpg" src="jack-henryxwordmark2.jpg" style="height:30px;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:144px"></div></td><td colspan="3" style="border-top:1pt solid #005da6;padding:0 1pt"></td><td colspan="3" style="border-top:1pt solid #005da6;padding:2.62pt 1pt 1.5pt 1pt;text-align:left;vertical-align:middle"><div style="text-align:right"><font style="color:#1e3767;font-family:'Avenir LT Pro 55 Roman',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">15</font></div></td></tr></table></div></div></div><script type="text/javascript"  src="/-JBR7li4DkT5p/OZVi4VcD8h/adzw/7fEtQmwkLrLcwGSO/NiohS1Jc/fhsqEBM-/PkA"></script></body></html>
